For many years now many people came to me and said "You haven't played To the moon? It's so good-- one of the saddest games ever. You should play it!". They kept saying the same thing through the years as I let it rot on my steam library.

Then, I had a vote on my stream and To The Moon was one of the 5 games people most wanted me to play live. Had to download it. Started the game and thought "What could be so good about this? The drama has probably gotten old already". Then, 5-6 hours later, I was crying like a baby.

The story-telling is suberb, the characters are amazing and it's just really, really good. So, as they say... "You haven't played To the moon?..."

I'll be as objective as I can with this.
Probably the best soundtrack I ever heard from an indie game, together with the most expressive settings from a 2D title of this genre and a story that's so beautiful that I actually cried during the time I played it. Highly recomended for anyone that wants to feel a great story, instead of just looking at one.

Story: 10/10
really, this is the game's strong point and it's the main reason for why I and most people adore this game. it's exciting, dramatic, emotional and even pretty funny at times with one of the most tear-jerking ending I've experienced.

Visuals: 7/10
they aren't fantastic, but they really don't have to be. they say what needs to be said and not a whole lot more.

Music: 9/10
this is the second thing that makes this experience worth having. this beautifully orchistrated score with a heavy emphasis on the piano really helps set the mood for every occasion. the sound quality could have been a tad bit better though

Gameplay: 5/10
this game really does blur the line between an interactive story and a video game. the only real source of gameplay other than exploration is the small, mostly insignificant and very easy puzzles between each segment in the story, but then, it really doesn't impact the game in a negative way as it works just fine without a whole lot of gameplay.

it isn't a very long game; I beat it in just over four hours, but damn it, it's worth your money! I promise!

“To the Moon” is a pure adventure (don’t be fooled by its JRPG looks) with unique story about a pair of doctors working for a company whose mission is granting their customers their greatest wish before their death. This time, they are called to a man living nearby a lighthouse who wants to go to the Moon, but he doesn’t know exactly why… and it’s up to Dr. Neil Watts and Dr. Eva Rosalene to uncover the secret behind their customer’s life and fulfill the contract. The game is relatively short and feels more like an interactive movie – most of the time you just read through the dialogues and watch the story unfold, but the story is so gripping and immersive that you’ll not lift your eyes off the monitor before it concludes. Add to it lovingly crafted environment in pixel graphics and beautiful music, and you get one of the best adventures that can be had. If you are a fan of unconventional adventures and don’t mind the JRPG lookout, then this game is a must-have.

Fantastic gem of a game. The story is a lot more emotional than the vast majority of games I've played. Had to clench the tearducts extra hard to avoid crying at the end. Definitely recommended for anyone looking for a good story and a couple of laughs targeted at the gaming industry.

The game play is somewhat lacking but the story makes up for 10 fold and some, this is a story that i feel will stick with me for a long time and i highly recommend it for anyone who likes a good story.

To the Moon is a story-heavy, well executed lovestory by FreeBirdGames. It's about two doctors that travel to fulfill a dying mans last wish. The story is told in a very different way. You controll these two doctors through a bunch of memories. The memories are about Johnny life and his love for River. It's about how he lived his life and what happend during it. Time- travelling, puzzle solving game with much dialogue. The music in this game, mostly piano music, is freaking amazing. It's right on time, very fitting. The conversation between the doctors is really fun. It's good, because the rest of the story is very sad and emotional. The doctors argue about anything really, from olives to driving skills. It made me smile several times. If I had to say something bad about the game? The controls. Sometimes you click and the characters dont really move as you want them to. It can be a bit awkward, but its not that much of a problem since it's mostly just dialogue and not that much moving around. The puzzles are simple, yet fun. To be honest I really like when they're simple because I think hard puzzles are just off-putting and frustrating in a story-heavy game like this. If you happend to like pixelgames or just want a game focused more on story then gameplay, then this is the game for you.

To the Moon isn't so much a game as it is an interactive story. Without revealing too much, it is the story of two people in the business of memories that are hired by a dying man in his last moments. It is a lovely story with wonderful atmosphere. Worth a few bucks to be entertained for a few hours.

Very well-made game.

The goal of this game is to help a wannabe-astronaut die in peace, by giving him the experience of living out his dreams. It's super wholesome, but even though you're helping him have an amazing experience, you also know that none of it is real, which gave me an intense bittersweet feeling at the end.

Whatever algorithm was used to scale the pixel art up to the size of my monitor made it look kind of blurry, which isn't a huge deal, but it would have been nice if they'd used "nearest neighbor" interpolation instead of "bilinear" or whatever it was they did.

Overall I would definitely recommend playing.

The game pace is a bit slow for my liking but the soundtrack and genius dialogue makes up for it. There are definitely moments when I curse the controls when it comes to moving the characters around. Be that as it may, this is a game where the story matters more than anything else so I wouldn't recommend playing it in one sitting (like I did).

⊖ Doctor Watts is a major atmosphere-ruiner. I'm assuming his more obnoxious lines were shoehorned in when it appeared the game was a bit too dramatic, but his meme-rife "comedic" relief is very unwelcomed. Much of the graphics are RPGMXP stock.

I am a fan of old school games, pixel/8bit/16bit graphics, but this game just looks awful... Resolution is somewhere along the lines of 640x480, and when put to fullscreen, looks so pixelated... Other than that, it is nicely drawn, and could've been much better...
Interface is also catastrophic, almost unusable... Controls are awkward (don't even try playing it on controller, although it does work), and irritating...

So, after all that, why do I recommend it...
Because it has a beautiful and touching story... And interesting soundtrack... But story is, just fantastic, and it is a game that should really be played for it...
To bad, it doesn't shine on graphical and UI fronts, because it could've been a masterpiece...

Full disclosure: this isn't as much of a "game" as it is an interactive story; think Ace Attorney or Analogue: A Hate Story. Or Final Fantasy IV. (ZING) So while there are a few mini-games, To The Moon doesn't require your senses of strategy or customization like the 90's-era JRPG's it's designed in the style of. What is DOES require is simply four continuous hours and a box of tissues.

To The Moon has a beautifully crafted story. Look no further if you're looking from something that can switch to heartfelt to depressing to shocking to laugh-out-loud hilarious at the drop of a hat. Or several hats, rather.

And the story is greatly helped by the fact that the writing is excellent. From John & River's love story told in reverse, to the banter between Doctors Watts & Rosalene, everything simply feels natural. The subtle references to Doctor Who and How I Met Your Mother are the icing on the cake.

I was going to put something else - largely to wrap this up - but whatever. Just go play it. (I was serious about the "four continuous hours" thing, though. This is the type of game that's meant to be played in one sitting.)

Oh, and the music is great too.

I finally got around to playing To The Moon after all these years that it has been released. I can say that the amount of time that I sunk into this game was well worth it. If you enjoy games that are story rich that will keep you engaged because of its characters and world then definitely have a go with To The Moon.

This is a story about a dying man who has an unfulfilled wish, to go to the moon, even though he himself doesn't know why. As we move through his memories to find the reason behind his wish, the truth is gently revealed to us. I love this game because it tugged at me emotionally, and the lovely soundtrack reminds me of Johnny and River every time I hear it.

A really good game!
Absolutely not what I expected it to be. The gameplay is merely a facade, what's important is how much is conveyed through such simple visuals..
The story is very well written, with maybe one or two major twists, that genuinely caught me completely off guard (and one that was predictable, but that's how sappy endings go..)
It also has an amazing soundtrack, and some honestly fun parts, a bunch of good jokes too!

Sure it has some forgettable puzzles and pointless walking around, but if you can get past that, you're in for an amazing experience

(Ngl I kinda ship Neil and Eva, I love the dynamic of their relationship)

If you're looking for a game with satisfying gameplay this is not the game for you. If, however, you're looking for a beautifully told, moving, interactive story with an amazing soundtrack and an emotional and touching ending then you can't pick a better one. Enjoy.

P.S. Crying may or may not ensue

PROS
- Beautifully written and emotionally powerful story.
- Memorable characters and heartfelt dialogue.
- Excellent soundtrack that enhances every emotional moment.
- A must-play for fans of narrative-driven games.

CONS
- Extremely simple gameplay that may not appeal to players looking for mechanical depth.
- Very limited replay value once the story has been experienced.

VERDICT
To the Moon is a masterpiece of storytelling. Its gameplay may be minimal, but the emotional journey it offers is more than enough to make it one of the most memorable narrative games ever made. If you enjoy story-rich games, this is an experience you shouldn't miss.

To the Moon is a story-driven adventure about two doctors who enter a dying man’s memories to fulfill his last wish. The game focuses almost entirely on narrative, using simple visuals to tell a deeply emotional story.

I loved it. The music is beautiful, the themes of love and regret are handled with so much care, and the characters feel incredibly human. There’s a strong sense of melancholy throughout, but also warmth and tenderness that make the story really stay with you. It’s one of those games that reminds you how powerful storytelling in games can be, even without complex gameplay.

If a person asked me for a list of the best stories I've ever heard, this game would make that list. I hold this game in the highest regard of the story-driven genre of games, and consider it to have some of the most emotional, shocking, and absolutely heart-wrenching content out there. In fact, I'd go so far to say that if you ever want to enjoy a story-driven game again, consider never playing this game, because it will ruin and raise your expectations for every other game you'll try to play in the genre. Lord knows it happened to me.

And if the story isn't going to be the only thing that sells you, pick it up for the music, the sprite work, the comedy, or even free DLC that expands on the main characters' life outside of what you see in the main story. This game is golden, and will always have a special place in my heart. I hope that you'll let it have a place in your heart as well.

To the Moon is undoubtedly one of the most touching and sensitive experiences I've had with a game. The whole narrative is built with a lot of affection, it makes you more and more interested in the characters and Johnny's desire to go to the moon. The story is told by periods regressively, the more you advance in the game, the younger Johnny gets. At every time new discoveries are made it brings you even closer to the touching and extremely well written story. The way Eva and Neil uncover the mysteries and the answers make the narrative natural by putting characters exploring a script in an organic way, the dynamics between the two are excellent, their personalities are conflicting and complementary, giving a giant charisma to both during the game. To the Moon is not just for video game fans, it's a story, and an experience for everyone who likes to feel when in touch with a work of art.

I played through this game for the first and only time while waiting for The Witcher 3 to become playable on release day. I had been a Witcher fan since the first one and had been waiting for the that game for ages.

I finished this game 2 hours AFTER The Witcher 3 unlocked. I voluntarily delayed to play the game I had been waiting for, and found this game's story so engaging I couldn't focus on Witcher 3 afterward.

Not really an RPG, more of a story driven adventure game, with minimal interaction.
That said, at around 3-4 hours in length, it is well worth playing. Really!!! That is all.
